tools.name: upload_app
tools.description: Uploads an app to TestMu AI for mobile testing and displays upload status.

tools.name: generateHyperExecuteYAML
tools.description:
Generates a HyperExecute YAML configuration for running tests on TestMu AI's HyperExecute platform.

REQUIRED fields: project (language, framework) and testing (testDiscovery.command, testRunnerCommand)
All other fields are OPTIONAL.

Supports multiple languages and frameworks:
- JavaScript/TypeScri

tools.name: answerHyperExecuteQuery
tools.description: Answers questions about HyperExecute features, configuration, usage, troubleshooting, and best practices by searching through documentation.

tools.name: getHyperExecuteJobInfo
tools.description: Fetches and displays information about a HyperExecute job including status, test results, and progress.

tools.name: getHyperExecuteJobSessions
tools.description: Fetches and displays session information for a HyperExecute job.

tools.name: getAccessibilityReport
tools.description: Runs an accessibility scan on the given URLs and returns the issues found. Pass urls to start a scan, or testId to re-read a scan that already ran; exactly one of the two. Results arrive in issueDetails: allIssues (most-severe-first, one page at a time), rules (name and reference link per rule id, l

tools.name: analyzeAppViaTunnel
tools.description: Analyzes a locally running app for accessibility via TestMu AI tunnel.

tools.name: buildLocalAppForAnalysis
tools.description: Returns step-by-step instructions to build and serve a local web app and open a TestMu AI tunnel to it, so its accessibility can then be scanned with analyzeAppViaTunnel. It does not build, run or scan anything itself, and never includes the access key.

tools.name: getAutomationTestDetails
tools.description: Fetches detailed information about an automation test by ID

tools.name: getAutomationTestCommandLogs
tools.description: Fetches command logs for a specific automation test

tools.name: getAutomationTestNetworkLogs
tools.description: Fetches network logs for a specific automation test

tools.name: getAutomationTestBrowserConsoleLogs
tools.description: Fetches Browser Console logs for a specific automation test. Note: Not available for mobile app automation tests.

tools.name: getAutomationTestSeleniumLogs
tools.description: Fetches Selenium logs (web), Appium logs (mobile/Appium), or instrumentation logs (mobile/XCUI/Espresso) for a specific automation test. Automatically detects XCUI and Espresso tests and fetches the correct log type.

tools.name: automationQuery
tools.description: Read-only query of TestMu AI automation resources: list builds, get one build, list the sessions in a build, fetch test details, and retrieve test logs (command, network, console, selenium, instrumentation). Every combination works on platform "web" or "app": build list or get, session list or get,

tools.name: updateBuild
tools.description: Renames a TestMu AI web automation build. Overwrites the current build name.

tools.name: stopBuild
tools.description: Stops every running test in a TestMu AI web automation build. Running sessions end immediately.

tools.name: deleteBuild
tools.description: Permanently deletes a TestMu AI web automation build and its test results. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: triggerSuiteRun
tools.description: Triggers a phone call test run for a specific suite. This will initiate phone calls for all scenarios configured in the suite.

tools.name: getSuiteOverview
tools.description: Gets comprehensive suite overview for a project including run counts, latest status, scores, schedule information, and active calls.

tools.name: getSupportedPlatforms
tools.description: Lists the OS, browser and device combinations TestMu AI supports, to find valid os, browser and version values for a test configuration. With no filters it returns a compact summary: each desktop OS with its browsers (version count, newest and oldest) and resolutions, and each mobile platform with i

tools.name: listTunnels
tools.description: Retrieve all active TestMu AI tunnel connections for the account. Useful for checking which tunnels are running before starting a new one or debugging local testing connectivity.

tools.name: stopTunnel
tools.description: Terminate a specific active tunnel connection by tunnel ID. Use this to clean up tunnels that are no longer needed.

tools.name: deleteSession
tools.description: Permanently delete a specific automation test session from TestMu AI by session ID.

tools.name: updateSession
tools.description: Update the name or pass/fail status of a test session. Use status_ind to mark tests as passed, failed, error, or skipped from your test framework.

tools.name: stopSession
tools.description: Stop an active running test session on TestMu AI.

tools.name: getSessionScreenshots
tools.description: Retrieve command-by-command screenshots captured during a test session. Returns screenshot URLs for each step. Web automation (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress) only: an app automation session returns not found; listMobileSessions carries the video and screenshot links of app sessions.

tools.name: getSessionVideo
tools.description: Retrieve the video recording URL for a completed test session. Web automation (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress) only: an app automation session returns not found; listMobileSessions carries the video and screenshot links of app sessions.

tools.name: getSessionV2CommandLogs
tools.description: Retrieve v2 command execution logs for a test session. Returns structured JSON with enhanced detail compared to v1 logs. Web automation (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress) only: an app automation session returns not found; listMobileSessions carries the video and screenshot links of app sessions.

tools.name: getSessionV2SeleniumLogs
tools.description: Retrieve v2 Selenium/WebDriver grid request and response logs for a test session. Web automation (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress) only: an app automation session returns not found; listMobileSessions carries the video and screenshot links of app sessions.

tools.name: postSessionExceptions
tools.description: Upload exception/error logs from the client machine for a test session, by session ID. Use this to attach assertion failures or unexpected errors to a session. The result reads the test's exceptions back to confirm they were stored. The automation dashboard may not show exceptions uploaded this way

tools.name: postTestExceptions
tools.description: Upload exception logs for a specific test (by test ID) rather than by session ID. The result reads the test's exceptions back to confirm they were stored. The automation dashboard may not show exceptions uploaded this way after the test ended.

tools.name: getLiveSessionLogs
tools.description: Retrieve the request and response log of a test session, while it runs or after it ends. Web automation (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress) only: an app automation session returns not found; listMobileSessions carries the video and screenshot links of app sessions.

tools.name: getOrgConcurrency
tools.description: Retrieve the current concurrency usage and limits for the organization on web automation (Selenium/Cypress).

tools.name: getAnalyticsData
tools.description: Summarises web automation test results in a date range: total tests, passed, failed, completed without a pass/fail mark, pass rate (passed over all tests, as the Insights page shows it), pass rate over tests marked passed or failed, average duration and distinct builds, grouped by status, browser, o

tools.name: getFlakyTests
tools.description: Lists tests that the insights engine marks as flaky (passing and failing intermittently) in a date range, with each test's flake rate, build and environment. Returns only flaky tests, plus how many tests were scanned. Flakiness is only computed for about the last 7 days of tests; the response says h

tools.name: getTestTrends
tools.description: Daily trend of web automation test results in a date range: for each day, total tests, passed, failed, completed without a pass/fail mark, pass rate (passed over all tests), pass rate over tests marked passed or failed, and average duration.

tools.name: getAnalyticsErrors
tools.description: Summarises failed and errored web automation tests in a date range: counts by failure category and by status, and the failing tests themselves with build and environment. Failure categories exist only for about the last 7 days of tests; older failures are counted as uncategorised.

tools.name: deletePrerunFile
tools.description: Delete an uploaded prerun file by stored TestMu AI file path.

tools.name: deleteUserFile
tools.description: Delete an uploaded user file by stored TestMu AI file path.

tools.name: listUploadedApps
tools.description: Retrieve all apps uploaded to TestMu AI for mobile testing. Use type=android/ios for real devices, emulator/simulator for virtual devices.

tools.name: deleteUploadedApps
tools.description: Delete one or more uploaded apps from TestMu AI by their app IDs.

tools.name: uploadAppVirtualDevice
tools.description: Upload an app (APK for emulator, IPA for simulator) to TestMu AI for virtual device (emulator/simulator) testing.

tools.name: listDevicesForTesting
tools.description: Lists the real devices available on TestMu AI for mobile app testing, 50 per page by default. Filter by region, OS, device name or OS version, and page with limit and offset. The text gives the total that matched.

tools.name: getMobileCapabilityGenerator
tools.description: Retrieve capability generation data for mobile automation test configuration.

tools.name: listMobileBuilds
tools.description: Lists mobile app automation builds, newest first, 10 per page by default. Page with limit and offset; the result gives the total the API reports. The API returns only builds from the last 90 days, so total can be higher than the builds you can page through.

tools.name: listMobileSessions
tools.description: Lists mobile app automation sessions (tests), newest first, 10 per page by default, with their video, screenshot and log links. Page with limit and offset, or filter by buildId or status; the result gives the total the API reports.

tools.name: getMobileConcurrency
tools.description: Retrieve the current concurrency usage and limits for mobile automation (real device testing).

tools.name: checkAppProcessingStatus
tools.description: Check whether an uploaded app has been processed and is ready for features like image injection, network logs, and screenshot unblock on real devices. tools.description: List all Test Manager projects the authenticated user is allowed to see. Supports keyword search and pagination.

tools.name: tm_get_test_cases
tools.description: Find test cases in a project by filters (folder, priority, automation status, type, tags) and/or search (matches test case ID like TC-123, or title; minimum 3 characters) — returns summaries. tools.name: tm_list_folders

Test Manager keeps three folder types: Test Cases and Test Runs folders (per project — pass project_id) and Modules folders (organization-level, since modules are shared across projects — no project_id needed). Pick with the tree parameter (default: test-cases). New test-case/test

tools.name: tm_list_modules

Reference a module by id when creating or editing a test case to include its steps (the Module itself is never changed).

tools.name: tm_list_configurations

To apply one to a run, pass the configuration's TOP-LEVEL id to tm_create_test_run or tm_update_test_run as configuration_id (NOT the nested environments[].environment_id). Pass run_type to see only the configurations

tools.name: tm_get_test_runs
tools.description: Pass run_id to get one test run's detail plus its result summary (instance counts by status — passed / failed / skipped / not started / in progress — and pass rate). Otherwise pass project_id to list runs with optional filters. Every returned run carries run_type ("kaneai" or "manual") identifying K

tools.name: tm_get_milestone
tools.description: Pass milestone_id to get one milestone's detail and live completion progress. Otherwise pass project_id to list the project's milestones.

tools.name: tm_get_coverage_summary
tools.description: Test coverage for a project, overall and per folder, computed live from the project's test cases (matches the Test Cases screen). Also answers requirement and traceability coverage: pass jira_id (any Jira issue key, e.g. TE-123: a requirement, user story, epic, ticket or bug) to get that item's test

tools.name: tm_create_project

tools.name: tm_update_project

tools.name: tm_create_folder

tools.name: tm_update_folder

Moves of test-cases/test-runs folders require project_id; module folders need none.

tools.name: tm_generate_test_cases
tools.description: Generate structured test cases from a requirement or prompt using the Test Manager AI generator (applies the project's Memory Layer — Project & Org Instructions — automatically) and file them into the chosen folder. Requirement documents, specs, spreadsheets or screenshots can be attached via files

tools.name: tm_create_test_case

tools.name: tm_update_test_case

tools.name: tm_create_test_run

tools.name: tm_link_jira_issue

Requires the Azure DevOps integration to be set up for the organization — otherwise a cl

tools.name: smartui_comparison_analyze
tools.description: Analyze one SmartUI comparison through a lens: consolidated (default), pixel, or dom. tools.name: smartui_screenshot_upload
tools.description: Upload screenshots to a SmartUI project as a new build, from local file_paths or from source_urls (fetched server-side, so it works without a client filesystem). tools.name: listHyperExecuteJobs
tools.description: List the account's HyperExecute jobs, newest first, with offset pagination and an optional status filter. The status filter looks at the 200 most recent jobs.

tools.name: getHyperExecuteJobArtifacts
tools.description: Retrieve all artifacts or categorized errors for a HyperExecute job or task.

tools.name: downloadJobArtifact
tools.description: Get an authenticated download URL (plus size/status metadata) for a specific HyperExecute job artifact. tools.name: getJobArtifactDetail
tools.description: Get details for a specific artifact within a HyperExecute job.

tools.name: getHyperExecuteStage
tools.description: Retrieve the stages of a HyperExecute task (cache/prerun/scenario/etc.). Pass a stageId to return just that one stage. Stages are keyed by their parent task, so taskId is required.

tools.name: getHyperExecuteStageLogs
tools.description: Retrieve logs for a HyperExecute stage. (UNDOCUMENTED - may change without notice)

tools.name: getHyperExecuteStageTasks
tools.description: Retrieve tasks for a HyperExecute stage. (UNDOCUMENTED - may change without notice)

tools.name: getHyperExecuteTask
tools.description: Retrieve details for a HyperExecute task by task ID. (UNDOCUMENTED - may change without notice)

tools.name: getHyperExecuteTaskLogs
tools.description: Retrieve logs for a HyperExecute task. (UNDOCUMENTED - may change without notice)

tools.name: getHyperExecuteJobLiveStream
tools.description: Stream live output from a running HyperExecute job. (UNDOCUMENTED - may change without notice)

tools.name: analyzeHyperExecuteJob
tools.description: Perform a full analysis of a HyperExecute job: fetches job info, sessions, traverses all tasks → scenario stages → console logs, and returns a structured report with test results, per-scenario logs, and pass/fail statistics. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: getAccessibilityReport, getSessionScreenshots, getSessionVideo, tm_get_coverage_summary, tm_generate_test_cases, tm_update_test_run, smartui_comparison_query, smartui_comparison_analyze, downloadJobArtifact · Private data: deletePrerunFile, deleteUserFile, tm_generate_test_cases, tm_create_test_run, tm_record_test_results, smartui_screenshot_upload, downloadJobArtifact · Public sink: upload_app, generateHyperExecuteYAML, postSessionExceptions, postTestExceptions, uploadAppVirtualDevice, smartui_screenshot_upload · Destructive: getAccessibilityReport, buildLocalAppForAnalysis, triggerSuiteRun, getSuiteOverview, stopTunnel, deleteSession, deletePrerunFile, deleteUserFile, deleteUploadedApps, tm_list_folders, tm_list_configurations, tm_get_test_runs, tm_create_test_run, tm_update_test_run, tm_record_test_results, tm_link_jira_issue, tm_link_ado_issue, smartui_comparison_analyze.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: getAccessibilityReport, getSessionScreenshots, getSessionVideo, tm_get_coverage_summary, tm_generate_test_cases, tm_update_test_run, smartui_comparison_query, smartui_comparison_analyze, downloadJobArtifact · Private data: deletePrerunFile, deleteUserFile, tm_generate_test_cases, tm_create_test_run, tm_record_test_results, smartui_screenshot_upload, downloadJobArtifact · Public sink: upload_app, generateHyperExecuteYAML, postSessionExceptions, postTestExceptions, uploadAppVirtualDevice, smartui_screenshot_upload · Destructive: getAccessibilityReport, buildLocalAppForAnalysis, triggerSuiteRun, getSuiteOverview, stopTunnel, deleteSession, deletePrerunFile, deleteUserFile, deleteUploadedApps, tm_list_folders, tm_list_configurations, tm_get_test_runs, tm_create_test_run, tm_update_test_run, tm_record_test_results, tm_link_jira_issue, tm_link_ado_issue, smartui_comparison_analyze

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
